component.name: Stellarshot
component.summary: Back up your files with encrypted snapshots

description.p: Stellarshot is a backup application for the COSMIC desktop. It keeps encrypted, deduplicated snapshots of your folders in a restic-compatible repository, so your backups remain readable with the restic and rustic command-line tools even without this app.

Set up several independent backups, each with its own folders, destination and schedule. A setup wizard shows exactly how much will be backed up, with excluded folders subtracted. Backups run hourly, daily or weekly in the background, catch up after the computer was off, clean up old snapshots under a retention policy, check themselves for damage, and notify you if something fails.

Getting files back happens inside the app: browse any snapshot, search it, see every version of a file, find files you deleted, and compare two snapshots. A dry run shows what a restore will do before anything is written, and an existing file is kept unless you choose otherwise.
Stellarshot is a fork of the cosmic-utils Stellarshot project and is under active development.

description.p: Estimate a backup's size without opening it, and a broader security and reliability pass across the web interface, restore and accessibility.

ul.li: An "Estimate Size" button next to Back Up Now shows a backup's file count and total size without opening it or asking for its password
A generated API token can now be copied with one click, and confirms before replacing one already in use
The web interface's password, port and allow-list fields validate as you type instead of popping up dialogs, and its address in Settings is now a clickable link
A hostile snapshot name can no longer be used to probe whether a file exists elsewhere on the machine, and a symlink at a backup's progress file path is no longer followed
Restoring into a folder where a snapshot expects a directory but a plain file already exists there is now reported as a real conflict instead of silently restoring nothing
The panel applet shows a failure, an overdue backup and real damage as three distinct icons, and no longer polls constantly while its popup is closed
Every icon button, checkbox and the two fields that most needed it now work properly with a screen reader or the keyboard alone
Comparing snapshots, browsing a large folder, or excluding deep folders no longer redoes the same work on every tick or renders unbounded lists

description.p: A full security and reliability audit, and the web interface actually reachable end to end for the first time.

ul.li: The web interface runs as its own systemd service, always reached over HTTPS, with a Start/Stop/Restart control and status in Settings
A new REST route starts an existing backup, the same as Back Up Now on the desktop
Repeated wrong passwords or tokens now lock an address out for longer each time, instead of the same short window every time
Changing the web interface's password, token, or allow-list now takes effect immediately, not just on the next restart
The repository password is wiped from memory as soon as it is no longer needed, and a crash can no longer write it to a core dump
A snapshot from a shared repository can no longer write outside the folder you chose when restoring
Importing a settings file from someone else can no longer run a command of its own
Opening a large file from a mounted snapshot, or downloading a folder, no longer reads it whole into memory first

description.p: Getting more out of a backup, and the start of a web interface.

ul.li: Choose a compression level when creating a backup
Mount a snapshot as a read-only folder, browsable and openable with any application
A History page showing every backup's activity in one place
Search for a file by name across every snapshot at once
The Compare tab groups changes by folder instead of one long flat list
Web interface settings, and a daemon with real password and API token authentication (still in progress)

description.p: Automation: conditions for when a scheduled backup runs, hooks before and after one, starting one when its drive connects, and a panel applet to keep an eye on it all.

ul.li: Browse a folder by size to choose what to include or exclude, like a disk usage tree
Download a file or folder straight from a snapshot, without restoring anything
Conditions for a scheduled backup: mains power, a battery level, not a metered connection, only a trusted Wi-Fi network or a VPN
A COSMIC panel applet with a status icon; closing the window now minimizes to it instead of quitting
Hooks: run a command or program before and after a backup
Start a backup as soon as its destination drive is connected, instead of on a fixed schedule

description.p: What is backed up, its history, and getting it back, and storage and credentials.

ul.li: Exclude by pattern or a file of patterns, and leave out cache folders and anything .gitignore covers
Pin a snapshot so cleaning up never removes it, however old it gets
Restore options: verify files by content, and choose how ownership comes back
A REST server destination (rest-server, rustic-server), reached directly without rclone
A bandwidth limit, and a password from a command instead of the keyring
Several keys per backup, and changing a backup's password from its own page
Append-only mode: rustic itself then refuses to delete a snapshot, a guard against mistakes rather than attacks

description.p: Seeing what is going on: status, history, and repository statistics.

ul.li: A status icon for every backup in the sidebar, and the time of its next scheduled run
An Overview screen: every backup, folder and storage location at a glance
Repository statistics on request, and a history of every run, failure, check and clean-up
A notification when a destination stays unreachable, instead of silence
Export and import of every backup's settings and history, never a password
The wizard sits beside the backup list and is resumable: Cancel offers Finish Later or Discard
Sign in to Google Drive with your own OAuth client instead of the one rclone shares with everyone

description.p: Fixes from testing the first release.

ul.li: Cancel stops a backup to an SSH server or cloud storage
Faster Google Drive backups: four uploads at once, and clean-ups that free space straight away
A backup in progress shows how long it has run and what it is waiting for
One press of Next checks a destination and moves on; a check that gets no answer stops after a minute
The size estimate written out as a sum, and the “Smart” setting explained exactly
Several independent backups, each with its own folders, exclusions, destination and password
Folders, removable drives, SSH servers, Google Drive and other rclone remotes
A complete restore: browse, search, versions, deleted files, compare, and a dry run first
Scheduled backups with retention, integrity checks and failure notifications
Import from Déjà Dup
